title: Not All Instructions Are Forgotten Equal
summary: I wanted to know why LLMs follow some instructions for a whole session and quietly drop others a few turns later. So I ran a small study: 244 cases of an instruction being obeyed or ignored, fit with a Bayesian hierarchical ordered-logit model. Some instruction types got followed about 10x more reliably than others, and at least one gets worse the more the model is reinforced on it. The intervals are wide and it's a single study, so don't read too much into it yet.
note: The benchmark behind it is open source, built on Inspect AI (UK AISI's eval framework): deterministic checkers plus a panel of LLM judges from different model families. Code's almost ready to release.
